summary: Farmersville sits on the dead-flat floor of the San Joaquin Valley about 40 miles southeast of Visalia, and at just 2.3 square miles it is compact enough that most of its 10,400 residents live within a short drive — or bike ride — of everything in town, yet the density of roughly 4,500 people per square mile keeps it feeling more small-town grid than suburban sprawl. The economy here is unmistakably agricultural; citrus groves and dairy operations ring the city, and the broader Tulare County ag sector is one of the most productive in the nation, which means employment options within the zip code skew heavily toward farming, packing, and related services rather than white-collar office parks. A median home value near $238,000 against a median household income of about $58,000 yields a price-to-income ratio around 4.1 — meaningfully more accessible than coastal California, though a poverty rate above 24 percent signals that even these prices stretch many local budgets. Summers are intense, with average daytime highs around 80°F annually and stretches well above 100°F in July and August, offset by roughly 9.4 hours of sunshine per day and mild, foggy winters typical of the Central Valley. The landscape trades dramatic scenery for wide-open sky: sunsets here aren't framed by ridgelines but by an unbroken western horizon glowing over flat agricultural land. Farmersville is, at its core, a small ag-economy town where housing is attainable by California standards but where the tradeoff is geographic isolation from major job centers and the relentless Valley heat.
